# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

/** Flag the person with a reason until a date: true once the row shows `shows` (the reason while
 *  the flag is in force; nothing when its until-date is already past, in which case the step
 *  counts as taken once no error has shown for a while). */
export async function flag(page: Page, personId: string, reason: string, until_: string, shows: string = reason): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = row(page, personId);
  const done = async () => (await shown(r.getByTestId('person-flag-shown'))) === shows.trim();
  const already = shows.trim() === '' || await done();
  await r.getByTestId('person-flag-reason').fill(reason);
  await r.getByTestId('person-flag-until').fill(until_);
  await r.getByTestId('person-flag').click();
  return until(page, done, r.getByTestId('person-error'), 'flag', already);
}

/** Set the person's approver: true once the row shows the user. */
export async function setApprover(page: Page, personId: string, user: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = row(page, personId);
  const done = async () => (await shown(r.getByTestId('person-approver'))) === user.trim();
  const already = await done();
  await r.getByTestId('person-approver-input').fill(user);
  await r.getByTestId('person-approver-save').click();
  return until(page, done, r.getByTestId('person-error'), 'set approver', already);
}

/** Undo the transfer that brought the person here: true once the row is gone. */
export async function transferUndo(page: Page, personId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = row(page, personId);
  await r.getByTestId('person-transfer-undo').click();
  return until(page, async () => (await r.count()) === 0, r.getByTestId('person-error'), 'transfer undo');
}

export async function exportStatement(page: Page, personId: string): Promise<string> {
  const [download] = await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('download'), row(page, personId).getByTestId('person-export-statement').click()]);
  const path = await download.path();
  if (!path) throw new Error('export produced no file');

  await r.getByTestId('person-flag').click();
  return until(page, done, r.getByTestId('person-error'), 'flag', already);
}

/** Set the person's approver: true once the row shows the user. */
export async function setApprover(page: Page, personId: string, user: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = row(page, personId);
  const done = async () => (await shown(r.getByTestId('person-approver'))) === user.trim();
  const already = await done();
  await r.getByTestId('person-approver-input').fill(user);
  await r.getByTestId('person-approver-save').click();
  return until(page, done, r.getByTestId('person-error'), 'set approver', already);
}

/** Undo the transfer that brought the person here: true once the row is gone. */
export async function transferUndo(page: Page, personId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = row(page, personId);
  await r.getByTestId('person-transfer-undo').click();
  return until(page, async () => (await r.count()) === 0, r.getByTestId('person-error'), 'transfer undo');
}

export async function exportStatement(page: Page, personId: string): Promise<string> {
  const [download] = await Promise.all([page.waitForEvent('download'), row(page, personId).getByTestId('person-export-statement').click()]);
  const path = await download.path();
  if (!path) throw new Error('export produced no file');

content.text:
People can now have an approver, and that user can approve or reject the person's PENDING claims the way a steward can. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V101__person_approver.sql`, adds an `approver` column to `person`. `Person` and `PersonRepository` now read it and have a method to set it.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/approver`, set up the same way as the existing flag endpoint. It writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<person> user=<approver>` to the audit file.
- **Approve/reject rule:** in `ClaimStatusChange.java`, a PENDING claim can now be approved or rejected by a steward *or* that person's approver. The existing checks still apply, so whoever opened or last edited a claim still can't approve it.
- **Screen:** a new `features/approver/approver.slot.tsx` adds the approver to each person's row, with an entry and a button (`person-approver`, `person-approver-input`, `person-approver-save`). A refusal shows in `person-error`.

**Choices the request left open**
- **Who can set an approver:** anyone except a viewer. I first thought this should be stewards only, but the test has uma set approvers and uma is only a clerk (the default role). This also means a clerk could name themselves as approver and then approve claims they didn't open or last edit. If only stewards should set approvers, the test would need to make uma a steward first.
- **Clearing:** saving a blank entry removes the approver. Names that contain spaces are refused, the same rule as for role names.
- **Transfers and clones:** the approver is not copied when a person is transferred or a sheet is cloned. The person flag isn't copied either, and the test expects an empty approver in those cases.
